title: 10 Black Friday ad examples & creative formats converting in 2026
summary: Explore 10 Black Friday ad examples and creative formats, with last season’s data, channel specs and a build calendar to plan on-brand campaigns at scale.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


US shoppers spent $257.8 billion online over the 2025 holiday season, and Black Friday creative now has to work on mobile first (56.4% of transactions) while standing out in a feed where electronics discounts peaked at 30.9%. This article covers 10 formats that convert, from the bold typographic offer to the overlooked post-purchase upsell. It also does the production math and shows how Superside's AI-native experts and AI systems keep that volume on brand.


For many marketing teams, especially in retail, the run-up to Black Friday is the toughest stretch of the year. Demand for creative multiplies while deadlines tighten, leaving little time to recover before the rest of the festive season kicks in.


For context: US consumers spent[$257.8 billion online in November and December 2025](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/01/adobe-holiday-shopping-season) , up 6.8% year over year. The peak days were even more concentrated. Adobe's December 2025 data put[Black Friday spend at $11.8 billion](https://news.adobe.com/news/2025/12/adobe-cyber-monday-hits-record) , Cyber Monday spend at $14.25 billion and overall Cyber Week spend at $44.2 billion.


**That means there's plenty of revenue up for grabs.** But getting your campaigns ready to compete for it can put even a well-prepared marketing team through its paces.


We break down 10 Black Friday ad examples and formats, when to use them and how to adapt them across channels without adding "cancel weekend plans" to the production schedule.


## What last year taught us about Black Friday creative formats


Before you choose your Black Friday ad creative formats, it helps to understand how people shopped last season.


**These six findings from last year offer useful insights:**


Finding Period What to consider for your creative


Smartphones accounted for 56.4% of US online transactions. Nov. and Dec. 2025 Make product details, prices and special offers easy to read on a small screen.


Mobile devices drove 70% of online orders globally. Cyber Week 2025 Review ads and landing pages together on mobile, so the offer stays clear from first impression to purchase.


Traffic from generative AI tools to US retail sites rose 693.4% year over year, from a modest base. Nov. and Dec. 2025 Keep product descriptions and offer details clear and consistent across campaign assets and product pages.


Shopify merchants generated $14.6 billion in gross merchandise volume (GMV), up 27% year over year, with sales peaking at $5.1 million per minute. BFCM weekend 2025 Plan for rising demand by building reusable creative concepts and adaptable assets you can roll out across products, channels and markets.


Peak discounts on electronics reached 30.9%. 2025 holiday season When competitors offer similarly deep discounts, the percentage off won't set you apart. Use distinctive brand cues, compelling product benefits and clear creative concepts to give shoppers another reason to choose you.


Social media drove 15% of global traffic to retail sites. TikTok accounted for 9% of that social traffic. Cyber Week 2025 Test creative suited to each social platform, including vertical video where relevant.


*(Sources:[Adobe Analytics' 2025 US holiday shopping report](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/01/adobe-holiday-shopping-season) ,[Salesforce's 2025 global Cyber Week report](https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2025/12/05/cyber-week-ai-agents-sales/) and[Shopify's BFCM 2025 data](https://www.shopify.com/news/bfcm-data-2025) )*


If you're still on the fence about video, Amazon's own figures may persuade you to prioritize it. Its[Sponsored Products video guide](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/guides/sponsored-products-video) reports a **67% higher click-through rate (CTR) and a 9% higher conversion rate** than campaigns without video, with CTR jumping eightfold among the 20% of shoppers who watch for longer than five seconds.


## Ten Black Friday ad examples and creative formats


Certain creative formats help you cut through the noise of Black Friday promotions. The list runs from straightforward, offer-led ads to product grids, short-form video and post-purchase creative.


The right mix depends on what you sell, where you sell it and what you need your campaign to achieve.


**The table below summarizes the formats that work:**


# Format Best channel Primary job


1 The bold typographic offer Display, social feed Instant legibility


2 Product grid Social, retail media Range and value at a glance


3 Countdown urgency Email, stories, display Time pressure


4 Before and after price Feed, retail media Value clarity


5 Anti-Black-Friday statement Brand social, video Differentiation through refusal


6 Gift-guide carousel Social, email Category discovery


7 Short-form vertical video TikTok, Reels, Shorts Demonstration and hook


8 Early-access exclusivity Email, retargeting Loyalty and list value


9 Bundle and stack Retail media, PDP Cart size


10 Post-purchase upsell Email, on-site Cyber Monday conversion


### 1. The bold typographic offer


(Source:[Adobe Stock](https://stock.adobe.com/images/black-friday-sale-promotion-banner-featuring-bold-typography-with-flat-fifty-percent-discount-offer-typography-against-dark-minimalist-background-with-dynamic-white-diagonal-lines/2221393812) )


**This is the most common Black Friday format because, at thumbnail size, typography is the only element that's reliably legible.** Think enormous numerals, a hard color contrast and minimal ornamentation.


The problem? Everyone and their dog uses it during Black Friday. To make your creative stand out, use your own brand typography, elements and colors, so the ad reads as distinctively yours.


Our[tips for effective banner ads](https://www.superside.com/blog/tips-for-effective-banner-ads) and[banner ad design](https://www.superside.com/blog/banner-ad-design) guide cover the design basics.


### 2. The product grid


(Source:[Dribbble](https://dribbble.com/shots/26840323-Fashion-Ecommerce-Category-Page-UI) )


This format shows many products with visible prices in a clean, modular layout. **It answers the real question every Black Friday shopper has: Do you sell what I want at a price I like?**


Grids are the easiest format to roll out across sizes and markets because they're modular by nature. They work best for companies that sell a wide range of products.


### 3. Countdown urgency


(Source:[Sleeknote](https://sleeknote.com/use-cases/black-friday-countdown-bar) )


A visible countdown timer, a stated end date or a stock-level cue drives urgency. **And urgency is the oldest lever in retail.**


If you use this format, note two things. First, fake scarcity damages trust and increasingly breaks platform rules. Second, countdowns date instantly, so build them as templated elements you can update rather than flattened artwork.


### 4. Before and after price


Struck-through original pricing beside the new price may be blunt, but it can be effective.


**This format is also the one most likely to be governed by advertising standards in your market.**


Check regional pricing-claim rules before you build your Black Friday ad set.


### 5. The anti-Black-Friday statement


(Source:[Dokan](https://dokan.co/blog/491730/most-viral-black-friday-campaigns/) )


Publicly opting out of Black Friday can help your brand stand out amid the sales frenzy. That might mean donating proceeds, temporarily closing your doors or refusing to discount. Patagonia's "Don't Buy This Jacket" ad, which asked shoppers not to buy anything, is still the best-known example.


**But the stance needs substance.** Audiences can spot a performative opt-out, so take this approach only if it reflects your brand's values and how you do business.


### 6. The gift-guide carousel


(Source:[Pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/500603314849563080/) )


A gift-guide carousel groups products by recipient, budget or category, which makes it easier for Black Friday shoppers to find a suitable gift.


**It narrows the options during the busiest shopping weeks of the year** and gives people a reason to explore your range.


You can also reuse the format: Simply update the selection as products sell out or new offers launch.


### 7. Short-form vertical video


(Source:[Pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/97953360640893481/) )


During Cyber Week 2025, social platforms drove[15% of global traffic to retail sites](https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2025/12/05/cyber-week-ai-agents-sales/) , with TikTok accounting for 9% of those social referrals.


**To reach shoppers on TikTok, start with the format central to its feed: short-form vertical video.** Use it to demonstrate a product, share a gift idea or explain a Black Friday offer. You can adapt the same videos for Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.


Open with a strong hook, use on-screen text and show the product within the first few seconds.


### 8. Early-access exclusivity


(Source:[Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/blog/8-awesome-black-friday-email-campaigns-you-can-steal-this-holiday-season) )


Give email subscribers or loyalty members access to your Black Friday offers before the general public. **It gives them a clear reason to stay connected to your brand** and can encourage purchases before the main sale.


Make the advantage obvious in your creative: Explain who qualifies, when early access starts and how to shop. Be specific about the reward, whether it's a member-only discount or the chance to shop limited stock first.


### 9. Bundle and stack


(Source:[Fast Bundle](https://fastbundle.co/blog/black-friday-promotion-ideas/) )


Encourage shoppers to buy complementary products together with offers like "buy the set and save." **This can lift average order value during discount season.**


Show the products together in your creative, make the savings clear and explain any conditions for getting the deal.


### 10. Post-purchase upsell


(Source:[Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/blog/post-sales-emails-turn-buyers-into-fans) )


**The opportunity doesn't end at checkout.** Someone who buys on Black Friday may welcome a relevant Cyber Monday offer, especially if it complements their purchase. Create ads or emails that suggest a useful accessory, refill or upgrade, and clearly show how the extra product adds value.


Use our advice on how to[create ads that sell on Black Friday and Cyber Monday](https://www.superside.com/blog/make-black-friday-cyber-monday-ads) to build a separate set of Cyber Monday creative for recent buyers. Tailor the products and messaging to what they've already ordered.


For more inspiration, explore our roundups of[social media ad examples](https://www.superside.com/blog/social-media-ads-examples) ,[Instagram ad examples](https://www.superside.com/blog/instagram-ads-examples) ,[Facebook ad examples](https://www.superside.com/blog/best-facebook-ad-examples) and[digital ad campaigns](https://www.superside.com/blog/digital-ad-campaigns) .


### A note on choosing between formats


**You don't need all 10 formats.** Choose based on your products, channels and campaign goals.


- **Broad product range:** Start with product grids, gift guides and bundles.
- **Premium brand or a single hero product:** Test short-form video, early access and bold typography, since a grid dilutes a hero product.
- **Any brand with repeat buyers:** Don't skip the post-purchase upsell.


## What separates the creative that delivers results


Whichever formats you choose, keep these four principles in mind:


- **Make your assets readable at a glance:** Shoppers should understand the offer on a small screen in one look.
- **Keep your brand recognizable:** Your Black Friday and Cyber Monday assets should look and sound like you. Use distinctive brand elements to stand out.
- **Design for sound-off viewing and fast scrollers:** Caption spoken content, and get to the point before shoppers scroll past.
- **Give each asset one clear message:** Focus on a single offer or benefit, with a clear next step. Extra claims dilute the main reason to act.


Our guides to[designing high-performing ads](https://www.superside.com/blog/design-high-performing-ads) and[advertising creative trends](https://www.superside.com/blog/advertising-creative-trends) go deeper, and[how to optimize Black Friday marketing campaigns](https://www.superside.com/blog/how-to-optimize-black-friday-marketing-campaigns) covers the campaign layer around the creative.


## The differentiation problem, stated plainly


Black Friday puts you in a difficult position. You're competing for attention when everyone else is, often with similar offers. Your competitors use the same channels, promote discounts over the same few weeks and reach for the same visual shorthand: big percentages, bold type and urgent messaging.


That makes it tempting to turn the brand dial all the way to "sale." **But if your Black Friday creative could belong to any brand in your category, it may drive sales without building recognition.** The answer is to make the promotion feel 100%[on brand](https://www.superside.com/blog/brand-consistency-enterprises) .


Here are a few practical ways to do that:


- **Retain your typographic and color system:** You can create more urgency without abandoning the visual language customers already recognize.
- **Give people a reason to choose the product, not just the discount:** Everyone can say "30% off." The product, benefit or idea behind the offer is where you create separation.
- **Give the campaign its own creative idea:** It doesn't need to be complicated. A distinctive visual treatment, recurring message or simple concept can make a collection of sale assets feel like a campaign rather than a pile of promotions.


The goal isn't to make your campaign look less like Black Friday. It's to make sure that, among all the other sale ads in the feed, people can still tell they're looking at yours.


Our[DTC branding examples](https://www.superside.com/blog/dtc-branding-examples) and guide to[brand consistency in retail and DTC](https://www.superside.com/blog/brand-consistency-retail-dtc) show how to hold a brand through a promotional period.


## Channel specs and design essentials


Use these guidelines to plan your creative, then check the requirements for your chosen placement and market before launch, because specs change.


Channel Specs or requirements to check What this means for your creative


Amazon Sponsored Brands video Landscape (16:9) only. 6 to 45 seconds, with 20 seconds or less highly recommended. Videos start without audio. Show the product early and make the message understandable without sound.


Amazon Sponsored Products video At least 7 seconds. Audio is removed. No slideshows, letterboxing or talking-head videos. Demonstrate the product in use, with close-ups that clearly show its features.


Short-form social video Vertical (9:16) video. Length limits and areas covered by buttons or captions vary by placement. Hook viewers immediately and keep key content inside the safe zone. Use sound where it helps, with captions for spoken content.


Black Friday banner ads and display Uploaded banners need specific dimensions and file sizes. Responsive ads combine separately uploaded images, logos and text. Keep banners simple and readable. For responsive ads, supply clean images and separate copy rather than putting everything into one graphic.


Email Layouts vary across devices and email apps, and images may be blocked. Put the main offer and a clear action near the top. Keep essential details in text, and test on mobile before sending.


*(Sources:[Amazon Sponsored Brands](https://advertising.amazon.com/resources/ad-specs/sponsored-brands-video) ,[Amazon Sponsored Products](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/guides/sponsored-products-video) ,[TikTok](https://ads.tiktok.com/resources/help/article/creative-best-practices?lang=en) ,[YouTube Shorts](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16041697?hl=en) ,[Google Display](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9823397?hl=en) and[Mailchimp](https://mailchimp.com/help/accessibility-in-email-marketing/) )*


For banner sizes and layouts, our[best practices for Black Friday and Cyber Monday banner ads](https://www.superside.com/blog/best-practices-for-black-friday-cyber-monday-banner-ads) and[free ad design templates](https://www.superside.com/blog/free-ad-design-templates) are good starting points.


## The production math nobody plans for


Consider a modest Black Friday campaign: five offers across six channels, in four sizes and three markets, with an initial creative set and one refresh.


**That's 720 assets, before you add a separate set for Cyber Monday.**


For most marketing teams, that volume lands in the same three weeks every year, while the team stays the same size.


Three steps help you manage the workload:


- **Build modular creative from the start:** Create reusable layouts and elements so you can adapt the core concept across sizes without rebuilding each ad. A good[design system](https://www.superside.com/design-systems) is key.
- **Agree on brand rules before production starts:** Make sure everyone understands your[brand guidelines](https://www.superside.com/blog/branding-guide) so the work stays consistent under pressure.
- **Secure extra creative support early:** Give external partners time to learn your brand and prepare for the workload before the Black Friday rush.


Our guides to[automating ad creative versioning](https://www.superside.com/blog/automate-ad-creative-versioning) and[digital ad production for enterprises](https://www.superside.com/blog/digital-ad-production-enterprises) cover the mechanics.


## The Black Friday creative calendar


Timing is the difference between a considered campaign and a panicked rush. **Here's a practical build calendar, working backward from the peak:**


When What happens Why then


July to August Strategy, offer architecture and concept development Good concepts take time to develop.


September Build the master creative and lock approved brand rules Approval often takes the longest, so get it done early.


Early October Produce variants for channels, formats and markets Volume work needs a locked master creative.


Late October Put early-access and teaser creative live Capture early shoppers. Adobe saw consumers embrace earlier deals in 2025.


November Put peak assets live and have your refresh set ready Ad fatigue sets in fast at high frequency.


Cyber Monday week Launch a separate creative set, including post-purchase creative Different audience, different job.


December Launch gifting and last-shipping-date creative The season doesn't end on Cyber Monday.


### Why September is the real deadline


Start in September to give your content and creative time to work. Search engines need time to index new content, and rankings rarely follow immediately. Paid ads also need time for internal approvals, pricing-claim checks and platform reviews.


**Teams that start in November aren't running a campaign. They're reacting to one.**


### Don't forget the back half


Your December creative deserves a place in the plan too. You'll still need gift ideas, delivery-deadline reminders and relevant follow-up offers for recent buyers.


Prepare these assets in October, before Black Friday takes over the team's schedule. It's easier to do thoughtful work then than to squeeze it in after the rush.
